drivingQuestion: From where is it derived that the fat and other sacrificial portions of offerings of lesser sanctity are subject to the prohibition of misuse of consecrated property?
outcomeNote: Both derivations stand as necessary (Abaye), and Rav Zevid's explanation of why the fatty tail is not forbidden food is adopted over Rav Ashi's, which is refuted by the misuse consequence.

segments.he: גְּמָ׳ מְנָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי? אָמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי: דְּאָמַר קְרָא ״כַּאֲשֶׁר יוּרַם מִשּׁוֹר זֶבַח הַשְּׁלָמִים״, וְכִי מָה לָמַדְנוּ מִשּׁוֹר זֶבַח הַשְּׁלָמִים מֵעַתָּה?
segments.en: «GEMARA:» According to the mishna, one who consumes forbidden fat of an offering is liable for misuse of consecrated property. The Gemara asks: «From where are these matters» derived? «Rabbi Yannai said:» They are derived from a verse, «as the verse states» that the sacrificial portions of a bull brought for an unwitting sin of the anointed priest must be burned upon the altar: «“As it is taken off from the bull of the peace offering”» (Leviticus 4:10). «But what, then, do we learn from the bull of the peace offering?» Everything that is specified with regard to a peace offering is stated with regard to this bull as well (see Leviticus 4:8–9).

segments.he: הֲרֵי זֶה בָּא לְלַמֵּד, וְנִמְצָא לָמֵד, מַקִּישׁ שׁוֹר זֶבַח הַשְּׁלָמִים לְפַר כֹּהֵן מָשִׁיחַ: מָה פַּר כֹּהֵן מָשִׁיחַ יֵשׁ בּוֹ מְעִילָה, אַף שׁוֹר זֶבַח הַשְּׁלָמִים יֵשׁ בּוֹ מְעִילָה.
segments.en: Rather, «this» phrase initially «comes to teach» a halakha about the bull brought as an offering for an unwitting sin of the anointed priest, «but it turns out» that «it» actually «derives» a halakha from that case, as the verse «juxtaposes the bull of the peace offering to the bull of the anointed priest.» It teaches that «just as the bull of the anointed priest,» as an offering of the most sacred order, «is subject to» the prohibition on «misuse» of consecrated property, as offerings of the most sacred order are called “the sacred items of the Lord” (see Leviticus 5:15), «so too» the sacrificial portions of «the bull of the peace offering,» including its forbidden fat, are «subject to misuse» of consecrated property, even though it is an offering of lesser sanctity and is considered the property of the owner before slaughter.

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: כְּעוּרָה זוֹ שֶׁשָּׁנָה רַבִּי, ״כׇּל חֵלֶב לַה׳״ – לְרַבּוֹת אֵימוּרֵי קָדָשִׁים קַלִּים לִמְעִילָה?
segments.en: «Rabbi Ḥanina said to» Rabbi Yannai: «Is that» derivation «that Rabbi» Yehuda HaNasi «taught unattractive,» that you derive a new one? He taught that when the Torah states with regard to peace offerings, which are of lesser sanctity: «“All the fat is the Lord’s”» (Leviticus 3:16), it serves «to include the sacrificial portions of offerings of lesser sanctity in» the prohibition against «misuse» of consecrated property, even though the prohibition is stated explicitly only with regard to offerings of the most sacred order.

segments.he: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: אִיצְטְרִיךְ, דְּאִי כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״חֵלֶב״, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא: חֵלֶב – אִין, יוֹתֶרֶת וּשְׁתֵּי כְלָיוֹת – לָא. כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״כַּאֲשֶׁר יוּרַם״.
segments.en: «Abaye said:» Rabbi Yannai’s derivation «was necessary, as, if the Merciful One had written» only the verse “All «the fat» is the Lord’s,” «I would say» that the «fat» of offerings of lesser sanctity, «yes,» they are included in the prohibition, but the «diaphragm and» the «two kidneys» of such offerings are «not,» even though they are also burned upon the altar. Therefore, «the Merciful One writes: “As it is taken off» from the bull of the peace offering,” to teach that even these portions are subject to the prohibition of misuse.

segments.he: וְאִי כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״כַּאֲשֶׁר יוּרַם״, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא: חֵלֶב אַלְיָה דְּלֵיתַהּ בְּשׁוֹר – לָא, כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״כׇּל חֵלֶב״.
segments.en: «And» conversely, «if the Merciful One had written» only the phrase: «“As it is taken off» from the bull,” «I would say» that the prohibition applies only to those portions that are found in a bull, and that «the fat of» a sheep «tail, which is not» found «in a bull,» is «not» included. Therefore, «the Merciful One writes: “All the fat» is the Lord’s,” to teach that the prohibition of misuse applies to all portions of offerings of lesser sanctity, including a sheep tail, which is referred to as fat in Leviticus 3:9.

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב מָרִי לְרַב זְבִיד: אִי אַלְיָה אִיקְּרַאי ״חֵלֶב״, תִּיתְּסַר בַּאֲכִילָה! אֲמַר לֵיהּ: עָלֶיךָ אָמַר קְרָא ״כׇּל חֵלֶב שׁוֹר וְכֶשֶׂב וָעֵז״ – דָּבָר הַשָּׁוֶה בְּשׁוֹר וְכֶשֶׂב וָעֵז.
segments.en: «Rav Mari said to Rav Zevid: If» a sheep «tail is called “fat,” it should be prohibited for consumption,» like forbidden fat. Rav Zevid «said to» Rav Mari: «With regard to your» claim, «the verse states:» “You shall eat no «fat, of ox, or sheep, or goat”» (Leviticus 7:23). This teaches that the Torah designates as forbidden fat only «an item that is» found «equally in an ox, and a sheep, and a goat.» Since the ox and goat do not have a tail that consists of a large amount of fat, the sheep’s fatty tail is not prohibited.

segments.he: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: ״חֶלְבּוֹ הָאַלְיָה״ אִיקְּרַאי, ״חֵלֶב״ סְתָמָא לָא אִיקְּרַאי. אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה, לֹא יִמְעֲלוּ בָּהּ! אֶלָּא מְחַוַּורְתָּא כִּדְרַב זְבִיד.
segments.en: «Rav Ashi said» a different explanation: «It is called “the fat tail,”» but «it is not called» simply: «Fat, without specification.» The Gemara objects: «If that is so» that the addition of a modifier indicates that the tail is not truly fat, then one who derives benefit «from» the tail «should not be» liable for «misuse» of consecrated property either. «Rather, it is clear» that the correct answer is «as» stated «by Rav Zevid.»

moves.summary: asks the scriptural source of the mishna's ruling that sacrificial fat is subject to misuse
moves.about: from where it is derived that the sacrificial portions of offerings are subject to the prohibition of misuse of consecrated property

moves.cueHe: אמר רבי ינאי: דאמר קרא ״כאשר יורם משור זבח השלמים״
moves.summary: answers from the verse about the portions of the bull of the anointed priest
moves.about: the verse on the portions of the bull of the anointed priest, brought as the source for misuse of sacrificial portions

moves.cueHe: וכי מה למדנו משור זבח השלמים מעתה?
moves.summary: asks what that phrase could teach, since the bull's portions are already specified
moves.about: what the phrase 'from the bull of the peace offering' can teach about the bull of the anointed priest, whose portions are already spelled out

moves.cueHe: הרי זה בא ללמד ונמצא למד
moves.summary: the phrase teaches in reverse — the juxtaposition carries misuse back to the peace offering
moves.about: the verse teaches in reverse — juxtaposing the peace offering to the bull of the anointed priest so that the lesser-sanctity offering too is subject to misuse

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה רבי חנינא: כעורה זו ששנה רבי
moves.summary: objects that Rabbi's existing derivation from 'all the fat is the Lord's' already suffices
moves.about: whether Rabbi Yannai's new derivation is needed at all, given that Rabbi already taught the same rule from 'all the fat is the Lord's'

moves.cueHe: אמר אביי: איצטריך, דאי כתב רחמנא ״חלב״
moves.summary: 'all the fat' alone would have excluded the diaphragm and kidneys, so Rabbi Yannai's verse is needed
moves.about: why Rabbi Yannai's derivation is still necessary alongside Rabbi's — neither verse alone would cover both the fat and the other portions

moves.summary: and conversely 'as it is taken off' alone would have excluded the fat of the tail, so both verses are needed
moves.about: the 'all the fat' verse, weighed as one of the two needed derivations

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה רב מרי לרב זביד: אי אליה איקראי ״חלב״, תיתסר באכילה!
moves.summary: if the tail counts as 'fat' for misuse it should also be forbidden for consumption
moves.about: whether calling the sheep's fat tail 'fat' — as Abaye's reading of 'all the fat' requires — should also render the tail forbidden for consumption

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה: עליך אמר קרא ״כל חלב שור וכשב ועז״
moves.summary: forbidden fat is only what is found alike in ox, sheep and goat, which the tail is not
moves.about: the forbidden-fat prohibition covers only what is found alike in ox, sheep and goat, and the fatty tail is not

moves.summary: offers instead that the tail is never called plain 'fat', only 'its fat, the tail'
moves.about: the tail is called 'its fat, the tail' but never simply 'fat', so the consumption prohibition does not reach it

moves.summary: on Rav Ashi's account the tail should also be exempt from misuse, which it is not
moves.about: if the tail is not truly called 'fat', then one should not be liable for misuse of consecrated property through it either — yet the mishna holds one is

moves.summary: concludes that Rav Zevid's explanation, not Rav Ashi's, is the correct one
moves.about: with Rav Ashi's explanation defeated, the sugya settles that Rav Zevid's answer to Rav Mari is the correct one
